{{Short description|English mathematician}}

[[File:William Crawley-Boevey.jpg|thumb|William Crawley-Boevey at [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]], 2014]]
'''William Walstan Crawley-Boevey''' (born 1960)<ref name="geneall">[http://geneall.net/en/name/2085073/william-walstan-crawley-boevey/ Geneall], retrieved 2015-01-16.</ref> is an English mathematician.
Since 2016, he has been [[Alexander von Humboldt Professor]] at [[Bielefeld University]], 
on leave from his position as 
[[Professor]] of [[Pure Mathematics]] at the [[University of Leeds]].<ref>[http://www.maths.leeds.ac.uk/people.html Academic and Research Staff] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017113730/http://www.maths.leeds.ac.uk/people.html |date=2017-10-17  }}, School of Mathematics, University of Leeds, retrieved 2015-01-16.</ref> His research concerns [[representation theory]] and the theory of [[Quiver (mathematics)|quivers]].

Crawley-Boevey is the second son of [[Crawley-Boevey baronets|Sir Thomas Crawley-Boevey, 8th Baronet]].<ref name="geneall"/> He studied at the [[City of London School]] and read mathematics at [[St John's College, Cambridge]]. He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1986 from the [[University of Cambridge]] under the supervision of [[Stephen Donkin]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=71333}}</ref> Before his appointment in Leeds, he held post-doctoral positions at the [[University of Liverpool]] and the [[University of Oxford]].

He was the 1991 winner of the [[Berwick Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/list-lms-prize-winners#Berwick Berwick Prize], List of LMS prize winners, [[London Mathematical Society]], retrieved 2015-01-16.</ref> In 2006, Crawley-Boevey presented an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited talk at the International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Crawley-Boevey | first = William
 | contribution = Quiver algebras, weighted projective lines, and the Deligne-Simpson problem
 | mr = 2275591
 | pages = 117–129
 | publisher = Eur. Math. Soc., Zürich
 | title = International Congress of Mathematicians. Vol. II
 | year = 2006}}.</ref> In 2012, he became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name="ams">{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|publisher=ams.org|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|accessdate=2017-01-28|archive-date=2018-08-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|url-status=dead}}</ref>
